questions.question: In Python, a for loop is used to iterate over the items of a sequence (like a list, tuple, or string).
A while loop in Python guarantees that the loop body will execute at least once, regardless of the condition.
A for loop in Python can iterate over a string, processing each character one at a time.
The break statement in a loop causes the loop to immediately move on to the next iteration.
The continue statement in a loop skips the remainder of the current iteration and moves to the next iteration.
When a loop in Python is not terminated by a break statement, the else clause (if present) will execute after the loop finishes.
After a for loop that iterates over a non-empty sequence, the loop variable retains the value of the last item processed.
In Python, the range() function returns a list in Python 2 and a range object (an iterable) in Python 3.
When a loop with an else clause is terminated by a break statement, the else block is skipped.
Modifying a list while iterating over it with a for loop will always produce an error in Python.
